predecessors.name: Kievan Rus'
predecessors.text: Smolensk, which went to Vyacheslav in the division of Yaroslav's lands (the rus dossier, Kievan Rus' page); the Smolensk page: 'The Principality of Smolensk was founded in 1054' (Smolensk page)

successors.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
successors.text: the principality, 'incorporated into Lithuania as the "Smolensk land"' in 1404

ledger.x: 1054: Smolensk becomes the share of Vyacheslav Yaroslavich, the first of Yaroslav's descendants to rule it.
1125: Rostislav Mstislavich becomes prince of Smolensk and the principality is independent.
1165: the princes of Smolensk take Vitebsk from Polotsk's line.
1168: Briachislav Vasilkovich recovers Vitebsk ('Briachislav Vasilkovich (1168-1175)'; 'Vitebsk later regained independence').
1186: Vitebsk again falls under Smolensk's influence, which angered Polotsk and Chernigov: 'In 1186, the principality of Vitebsk again fell under the influence of Smolensk.'
1195: the Polotsk and Chernigov princes who 'in 1195 marched against the prince of Smolensk' restore Vitebsk to Polotsk's rule.
1239: the Lithuanians briefly capture Smolensk: '1239: Lithuanians briefly capture Smolensk.
1240: Yaroslav Vsevolodovich expels the Lithuanians from Smolensk, which the Mongols spare: 'Although spared by the Mongol armies in 1240, Smolensk paid tribute to the Golden Horde'.
1294: Cliopatria widens Smolensk by about 34,700 km2 (Gomel in the south-west and Rzhev in the north-east).
1356: Algirdas captures Smolensk and Bryansk ('In 1356, Algirdas captured Bryansk and Smolensk'); the Algirdas page says he 'occupied Smolensk and Bryansk' without a date.

1359: Algirdas regains Smolensk and Rzhev and takes Mstislavl, after Ivan II's 1358 expedition had driven the Lithuanians out of Rzhev ('In 1358... drives Lithuanians out of Rzhev'; 'In 1359, Algirdas regains Smolensk and Rzhev and takes Mstislavl').
1359: the south-west band (Gomel, Orsha, Krichev, Mogilev, Kirov) passes to Lithuania.
1375: the north (Velikiye Luki, Toropets, Nelidovo) leaves Smolensk's shape for Lithuania's.
1401: Smolensk revolts against Lithuanian rule and recalls Yury (the last prince).
1404: Vytautas reasserts control and Smolensk is incorporated into Lithuania as the 'Smolensk land' ('Disestablished: 1404'); Lithuanian until Vasily III took the city in 1514.

wars.name: Smolensk's claims on Vitebsk
wars.outcome: Smolensk's princes held Vitebsk in 1165-1168 and again had influence over it from 1186; the Polotsk and Chernigov princes marched against the prince of Smolensk in 1195 and restored Vitebsk to Polotsk's rule.

wars.name: Treaty of Smolensk with Riga over Polotsk
wars.outcome: 'In 1227 Smolensk ceded Polotsk by treaty to the city of Riga'; the Polotsk page adds that 'For short periods, the neighbouring Principality of Smolensk also claimed control over some lands of the principality'.

wars.name: Mongol invasion (Smolensk spared)
wars.outcome: Smolensk escaped destruction in 1238-1240 ('Although spared by the Mongol armies in 1240, Smolensk paid tribute to the Golden Horde'); Cliopatria's Mongol Empire shape nevertheless covers its land from 1241.

wars.name: Golden Horde order against Ivan Aleksandrovich of Smolensk
wars.outcome: 'Ozbeg Khan orders Russian princes to campaign against Ivan Aleksandrovich over unpaid tribute'; the page gives no result.

wars.name: Moscow and Lithuania for Smolensk
wars.outcome: Simeon of Moscow entered Smolensk in 1352 and removed the pro-Lithuanian prince; Algirdas captured Bryansk and Smolensk in 1356; a Muscovite expedition drove the Lithuanians from Rzhev in 1358; Algirdas regained Smolensk and Rzhev and took Mstislavl in 1359.

wars.name: Vytautas's conquest of Smolensk
wars.outcome: Vytautas captured Smolensk in 1395 and Vasily I accepted the annexation in 1396; Smolensk revolted in 1401 and recalled Yury; Vytautas reasserted control in 1404 and the principality became the 'Smolensk land' of Lithuania.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the frontiers with Polotsk, Chernigov, Novgorod, Moscow and Lithuania are approximate throughout.
